answer: Every identity in the agent economy must lock a bond before it can act. When detection reveals clones—accounts that mirror one another's behavior or share a registration trail—slashing seizes the bond and burns it. This makes each sybil costly. At dawn, when new agents join, the deposit requirement sets the horizon of attack: a copy must fund every clone, so mass duplication collapses under its own collateral. The mirror of a fake identity is its unpaid bond.
